title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

opener.dateline: at Charles Shoemaker’s 5th of the 2nd month

body.p: I may just inform my health is much better than when I left home, and it has been very pleasant in having an account from thee, though not quite equal to a line from thee. I cannot give any account when my return to thee is to be brought about, but it the present prospect seems not likely to be soon. What I have had is from E. R. & J. R. who one of these I expect will be the bearer. If thou hast an opportunity, thou mayest inform Mary H. that I think Hinchman has been much favored. Sometimes I have felt well satisfied in being with him, and others my as though I was left almost naked, and destitute of anything that was good. Some families been visited I believe to good satisfaction. We are now at the Quarterly meeting of Abington, and expect to engage again in that labor when it is over please to give my love to our Children, and other friends as opportunity offers understanding Rachel has been to the doctor concerning her breast.
